text:
maya: Heads up 1 1 proposing consolidation of SIEM export retention defaults: Prod raw = 365d (strict), Prod redacted = 365d, Dev/Test raw = 90d, Dev/Test redacted = 180d. Rationale: keep full forensic window for prod while trimming dev noise. Need input on KMS + access workflow.

alex: Sounds sensible. Two big questions: (1) how do we let on-call or IR analysts access >90d data without creating broad permanent rights, (2) what changes to CMK policy + grants are required so exports remain decryptable across key rotation?

jon-p: For (1) I'd prefer a ticketed just-in-time unseal flow instead of broad role changes. Ticket creates ephemeral S3 copy with envelope key that has a TTL. Call it the "unseal_snapshot" flow.

lia: For (2) key policy owner is `service/security-kms`. We need to ensure our grant automation can create grants scoped to principal + operation (Decrypt) and that we record grant_id in the audit trail. Also: rotation requires envelope keys or encrypt-with-latest-cmk + rewrap on rotate.

secops-bot: NOTE: export playbook v0.9 located at https://redwood/internal/siem/export-playbook. New checklist item: include ticket_id and approver metadata in S3 object tags.

maya: Proposed access controls: - role `siem_unseal_requester` (can open ticket) - role `siem_unseal_approver` (must be 2 distinct people for >30d requests) - role `siem_export_reader` (time-limited, granted via ephemeral grant). All roles require enforced MFA and org scoping.

alex: Agree. We also need a machine identity (service principal) for the grant-maker automation. That principal should be explicitly allowed in the CMK key policy to CreateGrant but not listed as a decryptor. Grants give decrypt rights for the grantee only.

jon-p: Draft ticket template I'm using in the RFC:
```
type: siem_unseal
requester: <name>
reason: incident / vuln triage
scope: tenant id, dataset name, date range
requested_ttl_hours: <int>
approvers: [<name1>, <name2>]
metadata: { ticket: <ID>, poc: <email> }
```

maya: Important: include 'redaction_level' in metadata so pipeline can assert pre-export scrub if required. E.g. level=full | pii_mask | none.

lia: Audit requirements: every request + approval + grant_id must be immutably logged to WORM storage for 1 year, and KMS CloudTrail must be retained 13 months (per legal). We'll push both into our compliance bucket with strict retention.

legal-bot: Legal note: certain auth events and payment-related logs are subject to 365d retention and cannot be redacted beyond hashed IDs. Exceptions require documented legal approval.

alex: Action items I'm taking: (1) create mapping spreadsheet event_class -> default_retention + redaction_rules + legal_note, (2) PR for CMK key_policy addition for grant-maker principal, (3) stub infra for grant automation (initial TTL=72h).

maya: Infra notes: use envelope keys per-object and store encryption envelope metadata in S3 object tags. On rotation, the grant-maker should rewrap envelopes as part of a background job.

jon-p: QA: pre-export validation must run a redaction-check unit that rejects exports with high-risk PII tags unless approved. Also include a checksum of exported dataset and ticket_id in metadata.

lia: RBAC matrix: will add `org_allowlist` and `tenant_constraint` columns. Also add `requires_mfa` boolean. I'll circulate for review.

secops-bot: FYI: automated snapshot job (cron) will now add `ticket:none` tag for auto-archived snapshots. Manual unseal must replace that tag with ticket:ID.

maya: Sync request: let's do 30m review with infra + legal next Tue 11am PT. I'll send calendar.

alex: I'll draft the RFC tonight and include diagrams for KMS grants + envelope key flow. Expect PR link in thread.

jon-p: One implementation note: AWS CreateGrant returns a grantToken that can be used by the grantee within a short window; our automation should persist grantId for audit and rely on explicit GrantRetire for cleanup when TTL expires.

maya: Also add an FAQ about why we don't just extend dev retention: cost + risk of sensitive data exposure in test environments.

lia: final ask: ensure the export pipeline tags objects with `exported_by`, `ticket`, `redaction_level`, `event_class` for traceability.

alex: Good catch. I'll update the playbook and post the lifecycle example for the WORM bucket (retain 365d, deny delete).

maya: Thanks everyone. I'll add comments on the RFC and review the RBAC matrix once lia posts it. :white_check_mark:
